note: Artifact-level mind-map: every artifact placed heuristically from concept + tier + reading order. y = concept_order (timeline); x morphs from a single column (order) to concept clusters (x_spread).

concepts.key: Five axioms. Four are obvious. The fif
concepts.truth: Five axioms. Four are obvious. The fifth is not.

concepts.key: Euclid's fifth postulate held for two
concepts.truth: Euclid's fifth postulate held for two millennia. Then Bolyai, Lobachevsky, and Riemann asked: what if parallel lines don't behave?

concepts.key: A set collects things. The set of even
concepts.truth: A set collects things. The set of even numbers. The set of red objects. Most sets don't contain themselves — the set of even numbers is not itself an even number.

concepts.key: In 1931, Kurt Gödel fed mathematics to
concepts.truth: In 1931, Kurt Gödel fed mathematics to itself.

concepts.key: Each step makes sense. North side, hei
concepts.truth: Each step makes sense. North side, height one. East side, height two. South, three. West, four. Climb the perimeter clockwise and every transition feels valid — just stairs, just geometry, just one foot after the other.

concepts.key: Classical mathematics lets you prove a
concepts.truth: Classical mathematics lets you prove a bridge exists by showing that its absence is absurd. You never build the bridge. You never cross it. You just know, somewhere, it must be.

Classical logic has a rule: if a contradiction exists, everything follows. One false step and the entire system collapses into triviality. Pavel Florensky — mathematician, priest, executed by Stalin — rejected this.
Gödel's plaque. Russell's boxes. Escher's staircase. Florensky's sphere. Four wings of a single argument, radiating from a summit where the formula stands complete: QFE = F - λE(S) + φΔE(S,t).
